title: $j_!$ preserves bounded constructible complexes
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring and let $j\colon U\to X$ be an open immersion of
the setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. If $K\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_U})$ is bounded constructible
([sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]), then so is the levelwise extension by zero
$D(j_!)K\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ ([sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek],
[sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]).

proof.text: The setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] makes $X$ and $U$ finite type over the field $k$. The field has only the ideals $0$ and $k$, hence is Noetherian, and its one-point spectrum is quasi-compact. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to the structure morphisms shows that $X$ and $U$ are Noetherian. In particular their underlying spaces are Noetherian, as also recalled explicitly for finite-type schemes over a field in [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Every subset of such a space is retrocompact. Since the whole space is quasi-compact, taking it as the quasi-compact open in the definition of retrocompactness shows that every subset is quasi-compact. In particular, the inverse image of every affine open under the absolute diagonal of either scheme is quasi-compact, so both $X$ and $U$ are quasi-separated by [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Thus both schemes are qcqs. Consequently the open $U$ is retrocompact in $X$ and $j$ is quasi-compact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] to the closed subset $X\setminus U$ to obtain its reduced induced closed subscheme $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$. These facts verify the geometric hypotheses of the ringed open/closed lemma used below.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; topology.tex Tag 005L, lemma-constructible-Noetherian-space; schemes.tex Tags 01J3/01J4, lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme and definition-reduced-induced-scheme

proof.text: The module functor $j_!$ is additive and exact by [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek]. Represent $K$ by a cochain complex $C$; the exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] computes $D(j_!)K$ by the termwise complex $j_!C$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to $j_!$ in each degree to obtain $H^q(D(j_!)K)\cong j_!H^q(K)$. Choose $a\leq b$ with $H^q(K)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$, as supplied by [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. An additive functor sends a zero object to a zero object: the identity on its image is the image of the zero identity, hence zero. Therefore $H^q(D(j_!)K)=0$ for the same degrees; the cohomological bound is unchanged.

source.place: Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor, applied to cycles, boundaries and their quotient; blueprint proof first two sentences

proof.text: Fix a constructible $\Lambda_U$-module $M$ in the sense used by [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. By [def-sfb-constructible-module], choose a finite locally closed stratification $s_a:U_a\to U$ such that the restrictions of $M$ are locally finitely presented over the corresponding pulled-back rings. By the definition of immersion in [def-weil-closed-immersion], each $s_a$ is closed in an open subscheme of $U$. This subscheme is also open in $X$, so $r_a=j\circ s_a:U_a\to X$ is an immersion. On underlying spaces, write $U_a=V_a\cap F_a$ with $V_a$ open in $U$ and $F_a$ closed in $U$, and choose a closed $C_a\subseteq X$ with $F_a=U\cap C_a$. Then $U_a=V_a\cap C_a$ is locally closed in $X$. Together with $Z$ from step 1, these pieces give a finite disjoint locally closed partition of $X$ as in [def-constructible-stratification]. Every piece is constructible by the Noetherian clause of [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Empty pieces can be omitted.

source.place: Proof, finite stratification and reduced closed complement; topology.tex Tag 005L, lemma-constructible-Noetherian-space

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] for $A=\Lambda_X$ and the complementary immersions of step 1. By [sk-def-sfb-ring-object], the sheaf tensor product is the sheafification of the sectionwise tensor product. A map from it to a sheaf is equivalently a compatible family of sectionwise bilinear maps. Thus the ring multiplication and the action of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] are precisely the sectionwise multiplication and actions of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], in both directions, with the same action-preserving morphisms. For $g\in\{j,i\}$ with source $T$, the inverse image $g^{-1}$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] used in the ringed lemma and the pullback $g^*_{\Ab}$ of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star] are both the sheafification of the presheaf $T'\mapsto\varinjlim\mathcal F(V)$ over the same category of pairs $(V,\,T'\to T\times_XV)$ (the left Kan extension along the opposite of the base-change functor), so the canonical comparison of these colimits is an isomorphism $g^{-1}\cong g^*_{\Ab}$. It is compatible with sectionwise ring and module operations, so it identifies $g^{-1}A$ with the ring object $g^*_{\Ab}\Lambda_X$ and $g^{-1}$ on modules with $\operatorname{mapMod}(g^*_{\Ab})$. The coefficient comparison $\alpha_g:g^*_{\Ab}\Lambda_X\to\Lambda_T$ is an isomorphism of ring objects for every condensed $\Lambda$ by [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms], as also used in [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. These identifications are used in step 5.

source.place: Tags 09BN (lemma-open-immersion), 09AG (lemma-jshriek-zero), 09AH (lemma-ses-associated-to-open); ringed-site linearization: sites-modules.tex Tags 03DI and 03DJ; blueprint proof last three sentences

proof.text: Keep the notation of step 4. By clause 5 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], extending along the isomorphism $\alpha_g$ identifies the inverse-image module category with our coefficient module category. Under these identifications the right adjoint $j^{-1}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] becomes $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_j}\circ\operatorname{mapMod}(j^*_{\Ab})$, the module pullback $j^*$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], and likewise for $i$. The $j_!$ of that lemma and the $j_!$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] are both left adjoint to that functor. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] with the identity isomorphism of these right adjoints: the two left adjoints are naturally isomorphic. Its restriction identities $j^{-1}j_!\cong\mathrm{id}$ and $i^{-1}j_!=0$ therefore give $j^*j_!M\cong M$ and $i^*j_!M\cong0$ in the coefficient module categories.

source.place: Tags 09BN (lemma-open-immersion), 09AG (lemma-jshriek-zero), 09AH (lemma-ses-associated-to-open); ringed-site linearization: sites-modules.tex Tags 03DI and 03DJ; blueprint proof last three sentences

proof.text: The composition isomorphism of [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp] and step 5 give $r_a^*j_!M\cong s_a^*j^*j_!M\cong s_a^*M$. To compare with [def-sfb-constructible-module], use the invertible coefficient maps of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] entering the pullbacks of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] and clause 5 of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Relabelling an action along a ring isomorphism $R\cong S$ and its inverse are mutually inverse functors; they take $R^n$ to $S^n$. They also preserve a cokernel: its factorization property is unchanged under the inverse bijections on module morphisms. Thus a presentation $R^m\to R^n\to N\to0$ becomes one over $S$ with the same finite $m,n$, in either direction. Apply this to the presentations on the very same pro-étale covers supplied on $U_a$ in step 3, using [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented] and [def-sfb-finitely-presented-module]. Composing the presentation isomorphism with the displayed restriction isomorphism gives the required local presentations of $j_!M$ on $U_a$. On $Z$ its restriction is zero by step 5; for its pulled-back ring $R$, the identity cover and $R^0\to R^0$ present zero. The partition of step 3 consequently witnesses constructibility of $j_!M$ in [def-sfb-constructible-module]. No scalar-constant matrix condition is used.

source.place: Proof, restrictions to the original strata and reduced closed complement; local finite presentations as in the current bounded-constructible definition

proof.text: For every $q$, the module $M=H^q(K)$ is constructible by [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. Step 6 proves $j_!H^q(K)$ constructible, and step 2 identifies it with $H^q(D(j_!)K)$. In [def-sfb-constructible-module], constructibility is unchanged by an isomorphism: use the same stratification and covers and compose each presentation isomorphism with its restriction. Step 2 supplies the finite cohomological interval. These are precisely the two conditions of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. Empty $U$, empty $Z$, $K=0$, and the zero coefficient ring cause no exception: omit empty pieces and use the zero presentation on the remaining zero restrictions.
